title: Dual-icon toggle: pressflow contract, progressive disabled animation, and RTL theming
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: The dual-icon toggle (icon-left + icon-right variants used in compact toolbars) exhibits inconsistent press affordance, jumps when animating into disabled state, and misaligns icons in RTL. This causes perceptible layout shifts and an accessibility regression where screen readers do not announce state transitions consistently.

Goal: Define a stable pressflow contract for dual-icon toggles, implement a progressive disabled animation that avoids layout shift, ensure icons flip and padding mirror correctly in RTL, and add screen-reader-friendly ARIA updates. Create final token recommendations and a design spec with dev-ready motion values and fallbacks for reduced-motion users.

Why now: We observed increased regressions after the recent compact density changes (ENG-48xx rollout). Several customer bug reports mention toolbar flicker and confusion when disabling actions mid-flight. This ticket reduces regression surface and unblocks a Dedicated UI integration that pins toggle variants to runtime-1.18.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec for dual-icon toggle with explicit press/hover/focus token mapping published to Drive (link in comments)
Animated disabled state uses opacity + transform that does not change layout metrics (no width/height shifts) when toggling between enabled/disabled
RTL behavior mirrors icons and padding; visual tests included in storybook with LTR/RTL toggles
Reduced-motion media query respected; animations are replaced with instant state change for users who prefer reduced motion
Screen reader announces state change "on/off" or custom label via aria-pressed and live region updates
Dev handoff includes CSS variables, motion timing tokens, and 2 code-ready examples (compact toolbar + split action button)
Backward-compatibility doc describing how to opt older components into the new token set without visual regressions
design_decisions: Prefer composable tokens over baked CSS classes so Dedicated customers can override spacing and motion without forking components
Use transform: translateY(0.5px) and opacity crossfade for disabled animation to avoid reflow on most browsers
Stop using width animation for icon spacing; instead animate icon opacity and tint to indicate disablement
Mirror icons via CSS logical-properties (padding-inline) instead of direction-based JS flipping to keep render fast
Announce state changes via aria-pressed and a short non-intrusive aria-live polite region for contextual messages only when label changes
tradeoffs: Using transform + opacity reduces layout shift but might hide some micro-gestures; acceptable given accessibility gains
Moving to token-driven spacing increases initial migration work for product teams but simplifies long-term theming and Dedicated overrides
Logical properties approach relies on modern CSS; will include a small polyfill/fallback for legacy enterprise browsers in Dedicated builds
implementation_notes: Provide two storybook stories: DualIconToggle / CompactToolbar and DualIconToggle / SplitActionFallback
Motion values: duration 160ms ease-out for enable -> disable, 120ms ease-in for disable -> enable, reduced-motion fallback to 0ms
A11y: ensure role=button + aria-pressed toggles, add tabindex=0 for keyboard focus and keydown handler for Space/Enter
Test matrix: Chrome/Firefox/Safari desktop + iOS/Android WebViews, include RTL visual snapshots and reduced-motion snapshots
Add a small unit test asserting no layout reflow by measuring container offsetWidth before/after the animation in the test harness
